column1: # aes-r1.tsv -- AES round 1: pointer-free, non-blocking, non-mutating.
# Format (seven tab separated columns):
#   opcode  n_intin  n_intout  n_addrin  n_addrout  intin values  comment
# The four count columns are control[1..4] and are stated explicitly, not
# derived from the values: in the AES ALL FIVE control slots are inputs
# (EmuTOS aes/gemsuper.c:435 copies control[] onto a local buffer and never
# writes it back), and the dispatcher's marshalling is driven by the counts
# alone -- min(IN_LEN, I_SIZE) words in, exactly OUT_LEN words back out
# (gemsuper.c:436-445). A case that declares fewer output words than the call
# produces leaves the surplus slots poisoned, and that absence is the
# measurement. "-" in the n_intin column means "as many as the value column
# lists"; in the other three count columns it is an error.
# SAFETY, and this one is not a style rule. An opcode the machine does not
# implement reaches the dispatcher's default arm, which pops an alert box and
# WAITS FOR A CLICK (fm_show(ALNOFUNC, &opcode, 1), gemsuper.c:411-417). On
# the TT and on the Pi alike that is a hung run and a power cycle. Opcode 0 is
# the only unknown opcode that is safe to issue -- gemsuper.c:414 skips the
# alert for it. Nothing that blocks may appear in this file: the whole evnt_*
# family except evnt_timer, form_do, form_alert, form_error, fsel_input,
# fsel_exinput, graf_rubbox, graf_dragbox, graf_mbox, graf_watchbox,
# graf_slidebox, shel_write, appl_exit.
# Two more rules that keep a case honest, both with the same root cause:
# xif's int_in and int_out are UNINITIALISED stack buffers (gemsuper.c:430-432).
#   - Never declare more output words than the call actually writes: the
#     surplus is copied back from stack garbage, and a comparison of garbage
#     is a difference that means nothing.
#   - Never declare fewer input words than the call actually reads: the
#     handler then reads stack garbage as a parameter.
# There is NO reset between cases (core/runner_aes.h): the AES has no
# documented default state to restore, so round 1 holds only opcodes that do
# not mutate state another case reads. What that ruled out, and why, is in
# cases/COVERAGE-AES.md.
# A case id is the PHYSICAL LINE NUMBER and the file's CRC binds every dump to
# this exact file, so ANY edit -- an appended case, a fixed typo in a comment
# -- invalidates every dump already taken with it. Round 2 gets its own table.
# opcode\tn_intin\tn_intout\tn_addrin\tn_addrout\tintin\tcomment
# wind_calc (108) -- the geometry contract, and the bulk of round 1
# wm_calc is a pure function of type, kind and the four box metrics
# (gemwmlib.c:1807-1867); the spec states it outright: "wind_calc never
# touches the window list" (docs/api/aes/window-graphics.md, wind_calc).
# It is void, so int_out[0] is crysbind's ret = TRUE (gemsuper.c:85) rather
# than anything wm_calc computed. Outputs int_out[1..4], gemlib issues it as
# AES_PARAMS(108,6,5,0,0) (a_wind_calc.c:52).
# The rect is 100,100,200,150 throughout the kind sweep so that only `kind`
# varies. lb never grows, so int_out[1] is 101 (WC_WORK) / 99 (WC_BORDER) in
# every one of them; the interesting words are y, w and h.
# --- WC_WORK (1), one gadget bit at a time --------------------------

wind_calc WC_WORK NAME: title band

# Same call, same values, only the declared counts differ. These are the
# cases that measure the dispatcher rather than the window manager.

column7: OUT_LEN 0: nothing copied back, not even the return code

column1: # wind_get (104) on the desktop handle
# Handle 0 is the desktop window and is a real window: wm_init calls
# w_setup(ppd, DESKWH, NONE), which sets VF_INUSE (gemwmlib.c:1290, 205-213),
# so get_pwin(0) succeeds. Its rects are set at the same place -- CURR and
# PREV to gl_rscreen, FULL and WORK to gl_rfull (gemwmlib.c:1291-1294), i.e.
# the whole screen and the screen below the menu bar (gemgraf.c:423-424).
# OUT_LEN is per field, and it is NOT gemlib's 5: wm_get writes only
# poutwds[0] for the scalar fields and nothing at all for a field it does not
# handle (gemwmlib.c:1505-1599), and the rest of the local int_out is stack
# garbage. gemlib pre-zeroes aes_intout[3] and [4] before the trap for exactly
# this reason (a_wind_get.c:358). Here the count is cut to what the call
# actually writes instead.

column7: wind_get 0 WF_WXYWH: the desktop work area apps start from
wind_get 0 WF_CXYWH: whole screen, menu bar included
wind_get 0 WF_PXYWH: previous rect
wind_get 0 WF_FXYWH: full rect
wind_get 0 WF_HSLIDE: one word, w_setup left it at 0
wind_get 0 WF_VSLIDE: one word
wind_get 0 WF_HSLSIZ: the -1 "use default size" marker
wind_get 0 WF_VSLSIZ: one word
wind_get 0 WF_TOP: no valid handle needed
wind_get 0 WF_KIND: return code only, is it answered at all
wind_get 0 WF_NEWDESK: return code only
wind_get 0 WF_SCREEN: return code only, the address cannot be c
wind_get 0 WF_OWNER: AES 3.30 and later only
wind_get 0 field 0: no handler, FALSE
wind_get 0 field 13: a gap in the WF_ numbering
wind_get 0 field 21: past the last defined field

column1: # wind_find (106)
# wm_find is ob_find(gl_wtree, 0, 2, x, y) (gemwmlib.c:1767-1770), a pure
# read of the window object tree. W_TREE[ROOT] carries the desktop's CURR
# rect, which wm_init set to gl_rscreen (gemwmlib.c:240, 1291), so a point on
# the screen belongs to the desktop and a point off it belongs to nobody.
# Only points whose answer cannot depend on which windows happen to be open
# are here: the off-screen ones are nobody's on any machine, and (0,0) is the
# menu bar strip, which no window can cover (a window's rect comes out of
# gl_rfull, which starts below it).

column7: wind_find at the top left corner: the desktop, whatever is open
wind_find off the top left: nobody
wind_find one row above the screen
wind_find one column left of the screen
wind_find far off the bottom right: nobody

column1: # graf_handle (77) and graf_mkstate (79)
# graf_handle returns gl_handle and the four box metrics gl_wchar, gl_hchar,
# gl_wbox, gl_hbox (gemsuper.c:283-289). Those four ARE the inputs to
# wm_calc's border arithmetic, so this case is what every wind_calc case
# above is read against. int_out[0] is the AES's physical VDI workstation
# handle and, like every handle, may legitimately differ between machines
# (spec section 5).
# graf_mkstate is here only as an OUT_LEN 1 case. Its four output words are
# live input state -- xrat, yrat, button, kstate (gemgrlib.c:458-464) --
# which is where the operator last left the mouse, not an API behaviour, and
# with OUT_LEN 5 an unwritten slot is indistinguishable from a written one.
# What is left, and it is worth measuring, is that a void handler returns
# crysbind's ret = TRUE.

column7: graf_handle: the handle and the four box metrics wm_calc uses
graf_handle OUT_LEN 1: the metrics stay poisoned
graf_mkstate return code only: a void handler has to leave TRUE

column1: # evnt_timer (24) -- the one event call that cannot wait on an operator
# ev_timer(count) is ev_block(MU_TIMER, count/gl_ticktime) (gemevlib.c:134-137)
# and adelay turns a zero count into ONE tick (geminput.c:500-501), so it
# returns on its own after a tick and never waits for input. Void handler,
# so int_out[0] is ret = TRUE again.

column7: evnt_timer 0 ms: adelay makes that one tick
evnt_timer 1 ms: still under one tick

column1: # opcode 0 -- the only unknown opcode that is safe to issue
# gemsuper.c:414 skips the alert box for opcode 0 ("Ignore zero since some
# PRGs are this call") and returns -1 like any other unsupported opcode.
# With OUT_LEN 0 that -1 never reaches the caller at all, which is the
# sharpest statement of the copy-back rule there is
# (docs/api/aes/_dispatcher.md section 3a).

column7: opcode 0: the unsupported sentinel -1, and no alert box
opcode 0 with OUT_LEN 0: the -1 is computed and never delivered
opcode 0 with inputs: they are marshalled in and ignored
